title: Alone Together with the Dungeon Dive and Perplexing Ruins - Science Fiction and Other Stuff
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1tRJRX44zc

Daniel (@dungeondive) and Allan of Perplexing Ruins devote most of this episode to a genre both admit they're weaker in — science fiction — and the conversation is sharper for the inexperience.

They start with the imbalance itself. Fantasy dominates because dungeon crawling is universally legible: walk into a room, fight something, take the treasure. Space is harder because space is mostly empty. Allan turns that into an advantage mid-episode: in a fantasy hex crawl you generate terrain, weather, and features for every hex, but in space you roll once for an encounter and otherwise just fly. Point-to-point travel, no minutiae.

He then walks through a campaign built entirely from generators — *Monolith* (a Cairn hack) for characters and ships, *Star Dogs* for sector generation, *Screams Amongst the Stars* for world tables — and lands on two smugglers in debt to a Jabba analogue, on a frozen outlaw world, planning to break their own starship out of impound. Every beat came from character creation.

Daniel's counter-pick is *Space Aces*, 28 pages he had more fun with than *Starforged*, whose progress trackers he bounced off entirely. Its combat has no hit points — only gumption, which insults can drain.

----

Does science fiction genuinely play differently from fantasy at the table, or is it fantasy with a starship?
